title: Together AI expands fine-tuning service with more models, live metrics, and finer controls
gist: Together AI is repositioning fine-tuning from a black-box job runner into an experiment platform — live in-flight metrics, pre-flight dataset validation, tokenized-data inspection, early stopping with automatic refunds — while cutting training prices 30 to 70 percent. The technically loaded claim is Expert LoRA: putting adapters on Mixture-of-Experts expert layers recalled up to 89 percent of 200 newly injected facts versus 15 percent for attention-only adapters, and also beat them on MMLU-Pro 75.3 to 71.5.

themes.theme: Expert LoRA and MoE knowledge injection

insights.claim: In a Mixture-of-Experts model, over 90 percent of the parameters and most of what the model actually knows live in the expert layers, which standard LoRA fine-tuning never touches because adapters attach only to attention.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: If standard LoRA cannot reach 90 percent of a MoE model's parameters, most enterprise fine-tuning to date has been structurally handicapped.
insights.quote: In a Mixture-of-Experts model, over 90% of the parameters, and most of what the model actually knows, live in the expert layers.

insights.claim: In a controlled test teaching models 200 invented facts that base models could not know, adapters including the expert layers recalled up to 89 percent of the new knowledge while attention-only adapters topped out at 15 percent on the same model.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: A roughly 6x gap in knowledge injection reopens the case for fine-tuning versus RAG for proprietary-knowledge applications.

insights.claim: Expert adapters also preserved more of the model's existing knowledge and won MMLU-Pro outright at 75.3 percent versus 71.5 percent for attention-only adapters, contradicting the assumption that deeper adaptation causes more catastrophic forgetting.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Getting both more new knowledge and less forgetting removes the standard objection to aggressive customization of open models.
insights.locator: They also kept more of the model's existing knowledge

insights.claim: The mechanism behind the gap is routing collapse: with attention-only adapters a growing share of routed experts falls out of use during fine-tuning, while expert adapters keep the whole mixture engaged.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Names a concrete failure mode teams can diagnose, and explains why MoE models have underperformed expectations after customization.
insights.locator: The training dynamics explain the gap

themes.theme: Open-weight model cadence closing on proprietary

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 scores 88.2 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, within one point of the leading proprietary models, cited as evidence that open-weight models now reach frontier performance on agentic coding tasks.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: A one-point gap on a leading agentic benchmark undercuts the pricing power of closed frontier APIs.
insights.locator: For tasks that need frontier performance

insights.claim: New open-weight models are arriving at an unprecedented pace with nearly every release raising the bar on quality or efficiency, creating a recurring integration burden that platforms absorb by handling architecture-specific complexity behind a single training API.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Rapid model churn makes model-agnostic tooling the defensible layer, not any individual model.

insights.claim: The newly supported model list spans a full size ladder — GLM 5.3/5.2/5.1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi K2.7-Code and K2.6, Qwen 3.8-27B through Qwen 3.5 variants down to 0.8B, and Gemma 4-31B and 4-26B-A4B — explicitly segmented into frontier quality, cost-performance, and on-device tiers.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight families (GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek) dominate the supported frontier list — a geopolitical concentration worth tracking in Western AI stacks.

insights.claim: For local and on-device applications the Qwen 3.5 family offers options ranging from 0.8B to 9B parameters, positioning small open models as the on-device tier.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Sub-10B open models becoming production-grade shifts some inference demand off datacenter GPUs and onto edge silicon.

insights.claim: Together is cutting training prices on most supported models by 30 to 70 percent, with the gpt-oss series seeing the largest reductions — gpt-oss-20b SFT falls from $1.50 to $0.40 per million tokens and its DPO price from $3.75 to $1.00.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: A 73 percent single-step price cut on fine-tuning shows compute-services pricing deflating faster than hardware cost — margin pressure across the inference/training service layer.

insights.claim: Across the published table, DPO training consistently costs about 2.5 times the corresponding SFT price on the same model, quantifying the premium for preference-based post-training.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: A stable SFT-to-DPO cost ratio is a useful planning constant when budgeting alignment work.
insights.locator: Here are some of the price changes

insights.claim: The stated pricing philosophy is that intelligence should be abundant and that systems and algorithmic cost reductions get passed through to users rather than retained as margin.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: An explicit pass-through policy means gross margin at neoclouds is being competed away rather than banked — bearish for service-layer profitability.
insights.quote: At Together, we believe that intelligence should be abundant

themes.theme: Fine-tuning becomes an observable experiment loop

insights.claim: Fine-tuning jobs now record loss, gradient norm and learning rate at every training and evaluation step and expose them live through API, CLI and dashboard, with multiple jobs chartable on one set of axes so a sweep reads as a single picture.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Platform-native experiment tracking encroaches directly on standalone MLOps tooling — a consolidation risk for point-solution vendors.

insights.claim: Early stopping halts a run when validation loss plateaus, keeps the best-validation-loss checkpoint as the final model, and automatically refunds every training step that was not used.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Automatic refunds for unused compute is an unusual pricing commitment that pressures competitors selling fixed training blocks.
insights.quote: That means you get the best model, not just the last one, and you don't pay for training that no longer helps.

insights.claim: Data processing was previously a black box in which chat templates, label masking and silent row truncation caused quality drops that were hard to trace, and users can now preview rows tokenized with the exact tokenizer and chat template — token IDs, token strings, per-token labels, loss-contributing spans, and truncation flags.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Silent tokenization bugs, not model choice, are named as a leading cause of failed fine-tunes — a practical diagnostic for anyone evaluating in-house training quality.

insights.claim: Dataset validation moved from inside the training job to a server-side check that fires as soon as the JSONL file finishes uploading, covering message structure, tool-call pairing, reasoning fields, multimodal content, preference pairs and sample weights, and reporting the offending example index.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Shifting validation left cuts wasted GPU minutes per iteration — small per-job savings that compound into meaningful utilization gains at fleet scale.

insights.claim: Per-example sample weights let users scale any training example's contribution to the loss, addressing the fact that modern datasets blend human-annotated and synthetic sources across domains that should not carry equal influence.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Data curation weight becomes a tunable knob — reinforcing that proprietary data quality, not model access, is the differentiator.

insights.claim: Sequence packing, which concatenates sequences to avoid wasted computation on padding tokens, is on by default but can now be disabled because with a small dataset packing leaves too few optimization steps per epoch.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: A non-obvious trap: throughput optimizations can silently degrade small-dataset fine-tunes, the exact regime most enterprises operate in.

insights.claim: Gradient accumulation support means users can train at any effective batch size regardless of GPU memory, with the effective batch equal to batch_size times gradient_accumulation_steps.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Removes a hardware-imposed ceiling on recipe replication, letting teams reproduce large-batch published recipes on smaller fleets.

themes.theme: Self-improving training loops at trillion-parameter scale

insights.claim: Adaption's AutoScientist automates the full research loop behind model training — searching training recipes, optimizing data, training and evaluating in a cycle — supporting both LoRA and full fine-tuning across open models up to 1 trillion parameters on Together's platform.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Automated recipe search at trillion-parameter scale points to a market where model improvement is bought as a service rather than staffed as a research team.
insights.quote: We have partnered with Together to run Adaption's AutoScientist full self-improvement training loop at up to 1 trillion parameter models.
insights.locator: Case study: How Adaption automates training

insights.claim: Adaption positions itself around continuous learning from live data and environments rather than static training and costly retraining cycles, organized around Adaptive Data, Adaptive Intelligence and Adaptive Interfaces.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Continuous-learning startups imply sustained, recurring training demand rather than episodic training capex spikes.
insights.locator: Adaption is a frontier AI research company

insights.claim: Together plans to make every intermediate LoRA adapter deployable while fine-tuning is still running, so evaluation can begin shortly after a job starts instead of after it finishes, initially for GLM-5.3 and then Kimi K3.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Collapsing the train-to-eval gap from days to minutes raises iteration velocity, which is the real bottleneck in enterprise model development.
insights.locator: Coming soon: a faster path from fine-tuning to inference

insights.claim: Intermediate adapters can be attached to an already running endpoint in a Multi-LoRA setup, avoiding the cost and startup time of a separate endpoint for every experiment.
insights.speaker: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
insights.so_what: Multi-LoRA serving amortizes GPU capacity across many experiments — a structural efficiency gain that lowers per-experiment inference spend.
insights.locator: As soon as the first adapter is saved

source_meta.author: Artem Chumachenko, Egor Timofeev, Jasmine Li, Ruslan Khaidurov, Nikita Smetanin, Sergei Vorobyov, Arseniy Belorukov, Den
